extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_short: drafting and filing U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and regulatory requirements for preparing, arranging, and filing provisional and nonprovisional U.S. patent applications (contents, filing-date rules, conversion/continuation practice, drawings, oaths/declarations, and handling of Information Disclosure Statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required by 35 U.S.C. 111(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for patent under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) shall include (A) a specification as prescribed by section 112, (B) a drawing as prescribed by section 113, and (C) an oath or declaration as prescribed by section 115. The application shall be accompanied by the fee required by law. The fee, oath or declaration, and one or more claims may be submitted after the filing date within periods and conditions prescribed by the Director; failure to submit them within such prescribed period results in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date is the date on which a specification, with or without claims, is received at the USPTO. Applicants may submit fee/oath/claims after filing under prescribed conditions (may require surcharge). If not timely submitted, application is regarded as abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application requirements (35 U.S.C. 111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application must include a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and a drawing as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 113; a claim is not required. The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification (with or without claims) is received. The application must be accompanied by the required fee (which may be submitted later under prescribed conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional application will be regarded as abandoned 12 months after its filing date unless timely treated as an application under subsection (a) or otherwise converted; provisional applications are not entitled to priority or the benefit of earlier U.S. filing dates under certain statutes (e.g., sections 119, 365(a), 386(a), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c)). Provisional applications should not include an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS); any IDS received will be returned or disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of filing date and no new matter rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of an application (nonprovisional) is the date the specification, with or without claims, is received in the Office. No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For design patents the filing date generally requires the specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 including at least one claim and any required drawings. Continuing applications must comply with the conditions in sections 120/121/365(c)/386(c) and § 1.78 to claim earlier dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application components (37 CFR 1.51 / 1.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete (nonprovisional) application comprises: (1) a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112, including claim(s); (2) the inventor's oath or declaration; (3) drawings, when necessary; and (4) the prescribed filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and application size fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete provisional application under § 1.53(c) comprises a cover sheet identifying it as provisional, a specification under 35 U.S.C. 112(a), drawings when necessary, and the prescribed filing and application size fees. Applicants are encouraged to file an IDS in nonprovisional applications (see § 1.97 and § 1.98); IDSs are not permitted in provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover sheet requirements for provisional applications (37 CFR 1.51(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A cover sheet for a provisional application must: (i) state it is a provisional application, (ii) identify the name(s) of the inventor(s), (iii) give the residence of each inventor, (iv) give the title of the invention, (v) give the name and registration number of the attorney or agent (if applicable), (vi) give the docket number used by filer (if applicable), and (vii) give the correspondence address. If governmental interest exists, include the U.S. Government agency name and contract number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cover sheet may be an application data sheet. The cover sheet information enables proper filing receipt and processing. Failure to include required cover sheet info may cause the Office to treat the filing differently (e.g., as a nonprovisional).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred arrangement and headings of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred order of arrangement for a specification (each heading in upper case without underlining or bold): (A) Title of the invention; (B) Cross-reference to related applications; (C) Statement regarding federally sponsored research or development; (D) Names of parties to a joint research agreement; (E) Reference to a Sequence Listing/table/program listing appendix on compact disc and incorporation-by-reference; (F) Statement regarding prior disclosures by an inventor; (G) Background of the invention (including (1) Field of the invention and (2) Description of related art); (H) Brief summary of the invention; (I) Brief description of the several views of the drawing; (J) Detailed description of the invention; (K) Claim(s) (commencing on a separate sheet); (L) Abstract of the Disclosure (commencing on a separate sheet); (M) Sequence Listing if on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These headings are the preferred layout suggested for applicant use; see MPEP § 608.01(a) for more detail. If an Application Data Sheet (ADS) is used, data in the ADS need not be duplicated elsewhere except in particular historical circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) control and inventor naming
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ADS is used, the data supplied in the ADS will control over elsewhere in the application for most items; however, the naming of inventors is governed by 37 CFR 1.41 (and for some pre-2012 filings, inventor citizenship remains governed by earlier rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrepancies between ADS and other parts of application will generally be resolved in favor of ADS, except for inventor naming which follows specific rules in § 1.41. Be careful to ensure ADS accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under subsection (a) may be treated as a provisional application, and a provisional application may be converted to a nonprovisional application, subject to conditions, prescribed periods, required fees, and possibly the submission of at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion requests require fees (e.g., processing fee per § 1.17(q) or conversion fee per § 1.17(i)), must be filed prior to specified events (abandonment, issue fee payment, or expiration of 12 months), and do not entitle the applicant to refunds of previously paid fees. Note: converting a provisional to a nonprovisional can cause the patent term to be measured from at least the provisional filing date — consider claiming priority instead to avoid adverse term impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued prosecution / continuation / divisional / CIP application rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A continued prosecution application (a type of continuation/divisional) may be filed under specified conditions; continuation-in-part applications and continuations/divisionals have different filing requirements. A continued prosecution application: (i) must identify the prior application, (ii) disclose and claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application, (iii) name the same inventors as in the prior application (except as permitted), (iv) include a request that uses the prior file jacket and contents to constitute the new application, and (v) will be assigned the prior application's application number for identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application under this paragraph cannot introduce new matter. Filing such application is construed to include a waiver of confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent of access by members of the public entitled under § 1.14. If naming fewer inventors than a prior application, a statement requesting deletion must be filed. See §§ 1.78, 1.103(b), and 1.125 for related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet filing date requirements and correction process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission does not meet filing date requirements, the applicant will be notified (if correspondence address provided) and given a period to correct the filing error. Failure to timely correct may terminate proceedings in the application and may result in disposal and partial refund of fees (less handling fee). Requests for review of such notifications must be via petition with the fee under § 1.17(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for continued prosecution doesn't meet paragraph (d) because the underlying application is not a design application, that request may be treated as a request for continued examination under § 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion after filing for missing elements (fees, claims, oath/declaration) (37 CFR 1.53(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date lacks the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, at least one claim, or the inventor's oath/declaration, the applicant (if a correspondence address is provided) will be notified and given time to submit the missing items to avoid abandonment. If no correspondence address is provided, applicant has three months from filing date to supply missing items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventor's oath/declaration may be postponed until the application is otherwise in condition for allowance if (i) the application is an original non-reissue containing an ADS identifying each inventor by legal name and mailing address, and (ii) oaths/declarations are filed no later than the date the issue fee is paid. This postponed timeframe is not extendable under § 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment or cancellation of excess and multiple dependent claim fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees (§ 1.16(h),(i)) and the multiple dependent claim fee (§ 1.16(j)) are not paid on filing or later presentation, the fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely pay or cancel will affect prosecution—monitor claim counts and pay required fees or amend claims before the Office's reply deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) — general requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to file IDSs in nonprovisional applications. IDSs must comply with content requirements (37 CFR 1.98) and timing requirements (37 CFR 1.97) to be considered by the examiner. No IDS may be filed in a provisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS that complies with both the content and timing rules will be considered by the examiner. Noncomplying IDSs (e.g., late or insufficient content) will have items not considered noted in the file; in certain situations the Office will allow a short period to supply omissions if the IDS appears bona fide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of complying IDSs (consideration marking)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IDS complies with timing (37 CFR 1.97) and content (37 CFR 1.98), the examiner will consider the documents like other items in the Office search files. The examiner indicates consideration by initialing adjacent to citations on form PTO/SB/08A and 08B or by stamping 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials, and returns a copy to applicant noting which citations were considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-English documents, the examiner may consider them in view of a concise explanation submitted and need not require a translation unless necessary. The examiner should not state that the foreign reference was only considered to the extent understood except in the limited, established manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncomplying IDSs and examiner marking
rubrics_metrics.description: If an item in an IDS fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.97/1.98, a line should be drawn through the citation to show it was not considered; items that do comply will be considered and appropriately initialed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where part of an IDS's content is omitted inadvertently, the examiner may give applicant ONE MONTH to supply omissions (no extension under § 1.136) if the IDS appears bona fide; otherwise noncomplying information may be placed in the application file but not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents submitted as evidence in reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted and relied upon by applicant when replying to an Office action (e.g., affidavits, declarations, patents, printed publications) need not satisfy IDS requirements to be considered, provided they are timely presented; consideration is limited to the portion relied upon as rebuttal evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documents need not be processed as IDS items; the record should reflect whether the evidence was considered. Example: applicant relies on three patents in reply—examiner may consider teachings relied upon even if IDS listing also included other references that did not comply with § 1.97.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information printed on patent from IDSs and examiner-cited lists
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation listed on PTO/SB/08A/08B and considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent. The patent printing will distinguish IDS-cited references from references cited by the examiner on form PTO-892 (examiner-cited items are marked with an asterisk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not provide classification information or incorrect classification data is lined through, the citation will be printed without classification. If an item is cited more than once (IDS and examiner form), it is listed once on the patent. If an item was considered but not printed, the file record will reflect that fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic IDS (e-IDS) filing via EFS-Web rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An e-IDS may be filed via EFS-Web by entering citation information in an electronic form equivalent to PTO/SB/08A and 08B. As of January 2007, e-IDS may include U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents and non-patent literature (NPLs). Copies of foreign patent documents, NPLs, and unpublished U.S. patent applications not stored in the Office's IFW must be submitted in PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual e-IDS may contain up to 50 U.S. patents/publications, 50 foreign patent documents, and 50 NPLs. Applicants may file multiple e-IDS submissions; if a fee under § 1.17(p) is required, one fee can cover multiple e-IDS submissions filed the same date if conditions (fee included with first e-IDS, later submissions state fee paid, all received same date) are met. Ensure accuracy of U.S. patent and publication numbers because examiners retrieve references electronically; incorrect numbers require subsequent IDS correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: e-IDS examiner processing and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: If e-IDS complies with § 1.97, examiners must consider the e-IDS and indicate consideration by initialing, signing, and dating the e-IDS form. The completed copy must be sent to applicant and made part of the official file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may use electronic tools to annotate and sign IDSs. An e-IDS may be added to a new or previously filed application and will be scanned into the IFW. Examiners should not require paper copies of e-IDS references for consideration of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and practical points for e-IDS submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one e-IDS is necessary and only a single § 1.17(p) fee is to be charged, the subsequent submissions must clearly state the fee was included with the first submission and all submissions must be received the same date. Non-electronic follow-ups may be treated as received the same date if deposited under certain mailing/transmission rules (Priority Mail Express, certificate of mailing, or facsimile with certificate of transmission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the e-IDS form will be scanned into the IFW and the e-IDS will be added to the application file contents listing and PALM/EXPO database. If the e-IDS transmittal letter is missing, examiners may request OPAP to obtain a printed copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings and program listings submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings, tables, or computer program listing appendices may be submitted on compact disc (CD) under specified regulations (e.g., 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 for sequence listings). If sequence listing is on paper it should be arranged per guidance and noted in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the MPEP subsections cited for detailed formatting and submission requirements. Only tables, sequence listings, and program listings may be submitted on CDs in some contexts; otherwise follow 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Models, exhibits, and specimens — general handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A model, exhibit, or specimen is normally not admitted as part of the application, although it may be required in prosecution of the application (37 CFR 1.91 and 1.93).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If required for prosecution, models/exhibits/specimens must be handled per the cited regulations; otherwise do not include them as part of the filed application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application drafting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application should preferably conform to the arrangement guidelines for nonprovisional applications. The specification must comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and refer to drawings where necessary for understanding the invention. Unlike nonprovisional applications, provisional applications do not require claims or an oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the preferred nonprovisional layout for clarity and to maximize usefulness of the provisional. Because the Office does not conduct substantive examination of provisionals, IDSs are unnecessary and will not be accepted.
